Make-goal Launch Proof

After writing a goal contract, /make-goal can now start the campaign itself. Say “launch”, and scripts/launch-tmux.sh opens a fresh Claude Code session in tmux session goal-<slug>, with Remote Control on and /goal as its first message. This one unedited take runs the launcher through six cases, then the whole flow through a real /make-goal session, then reads the results back from Claude Code’s own transcripts.

Findings

  1. Fixed: the skill guessed the launched session’s permission behaviour. In T6, make-goal told the user the session “will ask before it writes files”. The session actually used the user’s default mode, auto. SKILL.md:261 now says a launch without a mode uses the user’s default, and that the skill must not describe it unless it checked (commit f8658b9). The script did not change after the take: git diff 3120f91 f8658b9 -- scripts is empty.
  2. An unattended campaign can stall on an API safeguard stop. In T6, Claude Code’s safeguards stopped two replies with a false positive (“This sometimes happens with safe, normal conversations”, request req_011ChLQFYxKUXXbBv6SppGw8), and /goal paused until a message was sent. This comes from the model service, not the launcher. Remote Control is what lets you send “continue” from a phone.
  3. Folder trust is per folder. ~/mg-launch-test showed the trust prompt even though /home/exedev is trusted. In normal use the launch folder is already trusted, because make-goal ran there, so exit 4 should be rare.
  4. Session names are per tmux server, not per folder. Two projects with the same slug cannot both launch on one server; the second gets exit 3 with the plain command.

Not covered

  1. Remote Control was not opened from claude.ai or a phone; only its on-screen status was checked.
  2. Every launch used a private tmux server (MG_TMUX_SOCKET) to keep your own sessions untouched. Real use goes to the default server, which differs only in the -L flag.
  3. The timeout path (exit 5) was not triggered.
  4. Only the default basic cast went through /make-goal end to end; the four named casts were not exercised.
  5. One host: Linux, tmux 3.4, Claude Code 2.1.330. macOS was not tested.

Run it again

The script is scripts/launch-tmux.sh in carbonscott/make-goal. From a folder that holds .goal/<slug>.json:

git -C ~/.claude/skills/make-goal checkout casts-and-guard
bash ~/.claude/skills/make-goal/scripts/launch-tmux.sh <slug>              # default tmux server
bash ~/.claude/skills/make-goal/scripts/launch-tmux.sh <slug> acceptEdits  # with a permission mode
MG_TMUX_SOCKET=test bash …/launch-tmux.sh <slug>                          # private server, as in this take
tmux attach -t goal-<slug>                                               # watch it

# or through the skill: /make-goal <goal>, then reply "write it and launch"
Audit trail

One take, 19:16:26–19:30:14 UTC, no cuts. Before it I probed Claude Code’s screens and dry-ran the script; those runs found two bugs, both fixed before the take: a pane target that tmux rejects (=goal-x needs a trailing colon) and a Remote Control check that ran before the line appeared.

The orchestrating agent typed every input. Inputs that stand in for a user: the “Yes, I trust this folder” choice in T4, the /make-goal request and “write it and launch” in T6, and “continue” after the API pause. The grey “write it and launch” visible in the input box before my reply was Claude Code’s own prompt suggestion, not something typed.

Redactions: three Remote Control session IDs were masked with same-length * in the recording’s raw bytes. The finished page was searched for them afterwards.

The session-registry read-back was captured outside the recording. It also listed unrelated sessions on the host; only the test sessions are quoted.

During probing I passed /effort low as a first prompt to test whether slash commands run there. It saved low as the default effort for new sessions; I restored it to high (the earlier value) at once.

Cleanup: the test tmux servers were stopped and no test Claude process remains. Trust entries for ~/mg-launch-test and two /tmp/claude-1000/mg-untrusted-* folders remain in ~/.claude.json.
